```{r, message=F, warning=F}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Hardcode your exact metrics cleanly mapped out by timepoint
data <- data.frame(
  Patient = c("IF-03", "IF-03", "IF-04", "IF-04", "IF-05", "IF-05", "IF-06", "IF-06"),
  Timepoint = c("Baseline", "Followup", "Baseline", "Followup", "Baseline", "Followup", "Baseline", "Followup"),
  Raw_R1 = c(35432588, 36551023, 37207749, 39219392, 37953563, 34241541, 36173670, 36216213),
  Raw_R2 = c(35431588, 36551023, 37207749, 39219392, 37953563, 34241541, 36173670, 36216213),
  Mapped_Reads = c(49479369, 64396851, 64926012, 66244683, 71810494, 63532220, 67674071, 69807294)
)

# 2. Reshape data into long format for ggplot group mapping
plot_data <- data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Raw_R1, Raw_R2, Mapped_Reads), 
               names_to = "Pipeline_Step", 
               values_to = "Counts") %>%
  mutate(
    # Format Counts into Millions for elegant axis labels
    Counts_Millions = Counts / 1e6,
    # Standardize factors and clean titles for rows
    Pipeline_Step = case_when(
      Pipeline_Step == "Raw_R1" ~ "Raw R1 Reads (FASTQ)",
      Pipeline_Step == "Raw_R2" ~ "Raw R2 Reads (FASTQ)",
      Pipeline_Step == "Mapped_Reads" ~ "Successfully Mapped Reads (BAM)"
    ),
    Pipeline_Step = factor(Pipeline_Step, levels = c("Raw R1 Reads (FASTQ)", "Raw R2 Reads (FASTQ)", "Successfully Mapped Reads (BAM)")),
    Patient = factor(Patient, levels = c("IF-03", "IF-04", "IF-05", "IF-06")),
    Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Baseline", "Followup"))
  )

# 3. Create the final clean publication-ready bar chart
p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Patient, y = Counts_Millions, fill = Timepoint)) +
  # Place bars right next to each other
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, color = "black") +
  
  # Professional High-Contrast Palette
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Baseline" = "#1d3557", "Followup" = "#e63946")) +
  
  # Add specific decimal annotations right over the bar structures
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1fM", Counts_Millions)), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Stack the metrics vertically into 3 clear operational tracking rows
  facet_wrap(~Pipeline_Step, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  
  # Extend breathing room at the top of the panels so numbers do not get cut off
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Patient Sample Sequencing Metrics Profile",
    subtitle = "",
    x = "Patient Identifier",
    y = "Read Counts (Millions)",
    fill = "Study Stage"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray25"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, color = "black"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray93", color = "gray80"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
p
```

```{r, message=F, warning=F}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Create the dataset directly from your samtools output
data <- data.frame(
  Sample_ID = c("IF-03_Baseline", "IF-04_Baseline", "IF-04_Followup", "IF-03_Followup", 
                "IF-05_Followup", "IF-06_Baseline", "IF-06_Followup", "IF-05_Baseline", "IF-07_Baseline", "IF-07_Followup", "IF-08_Baseline", "IF-08_Followup"),
  Mapped_R1 = c(24739053, 32462972, 33121436, 32197707, 31759284, 33836467, 34902506, 35902036,37381329, 38029179, 36447634, 41552929 ),
  Mapped_R2 = c(24740316, 32463040, 33123247, 32199144, 31772936, 33837604, 34904788, 35908458,37281118, 37916497, 36314512, 41399315 )
)

# 2. Reshape and clean data for true vertical stacking
plot_data <- data %>%
  separate(Sample_ID, into = c("Patient", "Timepoint"), sep = "_") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Mapped_R1, Mapped_R2), 
               names_to = "Read_Pair", 
               values_to = "Counts") %>%
  mutate(
    Counts_Millions = Counts / 1e6,
    Patient = factor(Patient, levels = c("IF-03", "IF-04", "IF-05", "IF-06", "IF-07", "IF-08")),
    Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Baseline", "Followup")),
    Read_Pair = case_when(
      Read_Pair == "Mapped_R1" ~ "R1 Reads",
      Read_Pair == "Mapped_R2" ~ "R2 Reads"
    ),
    Read_Pair = factor(Read_Pair, levels = c("R2 Reads", "R1 Reads")) # R1 on bottom, R2 on top
  )

# 3. Calculate total height labels for the top of each stack
total_labels <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(Patient, Timepoint) %>%
  summarise(Total_Millions = sum(Counts_Millions), .groups = 'drop')

# 4. Build the plot using Facet layout to force side-by-side patient groups
p <- ggplot() +
  # position = "stack" works flawlessly here because Timepoint is the clear X axis
  geom_bar(data = plot_data, 
           aes(x = Timepoint, y = Counts_Millions, fill = Timepoint, alpha = Read_Pair),
           stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.65, color = "black") +
  
  # Distinct colors for Baseline vs Followup
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Baseline" = "#1d3557", "Followup" = "#e63946")) +
  
  # Shading modifier to visually split R1 and R2 vertically
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("R1 Reads" = 1.0, "R2 Reads" = 0.55), name = "Read Segment") +
  
  # Add total text labels perfectly over the vertical stacks
  geom_text(data = total_labels, 
            aes(x = Timepoint, y = Total_Millions, label = sprintf("%.1fM", Total_Millions)),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Group patients side-by-side horizontally using 1 row
  facet_wrap(~ Patient, nrow = 1) +
  
  # Extra space at the top of the panels so labels don't clip
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Aligned Paired-End Read Profile Per Patient",
    subtitle = "",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total Mapped Reads (Millions)",
    fill = "Study Stage"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray25"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), # Patient Panel headers
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray85"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    
    
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box = "vertical"
  )

p
```

## Paired Differential Intensity Analysis




```{r, message=F, warning=F}
library(GenomicRanges)


# 1. Install BiocManager if you do not have it already
#if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
#    install.packages("BiocManager")
#}

# 2. Install the limma package
#BiocManager::install("limma")


library(limma)

all_peaks_GR <- do.call(c, unname(peaks_list))

length(all_peaks_GR)==sum(lengths(peaks_list))

    
# 1. Force the list structure to flatten into a pure GRanges object
flat_GR <- GRanges(
  seqnames = seqnames(all_peaks_GR),
  ranges   = ranges(all_peaks_GR),
  strand   = strand(all_peaks_GR)
)

# 2. Now run reduce on the flat GRanges object 
consensus_peaks <- GenomicRanges::reduce(flat_GR)
length(consensus_peaks)




```

* how function `GenomicRanges::reduce` works 


```
Before reduce():
Peak A:   [100 =========== 200]
Peak B:              [150 =========== 250]
Peak C:                                       [300 ===== 400]

After reduce():
Result:   [100 ======================= 250]   [300 ===== 400]
```





```{r, message=F, warning=F}

# 2. Extract 'signalValue' for each sample mapping to consensus peaks

num_samples <- length(peaks_list)
num_peaks <- length(consensus_peaks)

# Initialize matrix with a small background value (1.0) for non-overlapping windows
intensity_matrix <- matrix(1.0, nrow = num_peaks, ncol = num_samples)
colnames(intensity_matrix) <- names(peaks_list)

for (i in seq_along(peaks_list)) {
  sample_name <- names(peaks_list)[i]
  sample_gr <- peaks_list[[i]]
  
  # Find overlaps between consensus bins and this sample's peaks
  olaps <- findOverlaps(consensus_peaks, sample_gr)
  
  if (length(olaps) > 0) {
    # If multiple sample peaks hit one consensus region, take the maximum signalValue
    signal_df <- data.frame(
      consensus_idx = queryHits(olaps),
      signal = sample_gr$signalValue[subjectHits(olaps)]
    )
    max_signals <- aggregate(signal ~ consensus_idx, data = signal_df, max)
    
    intensity_matrix[max_signals$consensus_idx, sample_name] <- max_signals$signal
  }
}

all_ones_rows <- which(rowSums(intensity_matrix != 1) == 0) # report rows whose columns are all 1. 
all_ones_rows
```





```{r, message=F, warning=F}

# 3. Define the paired experimental design

samples_meta <- data.frame(
  SampleID = colnames(intensity_matrix)
)

# Extract Metadata: Condition (Baseline vs Followup) and Patient ID (IF-03 to IF-08)
samples_meta$Condition <- ifelse(grepl("Baseline", samples_meta$SampleID), "Baseline", "Followup")
samples_meta$Patient   <- sub("_.*", "", samples_meta$SampleID)

# Ensure they are factors
samples_meta$Condition <- factor(samples_meta$Condition, levels = c("Baseline", "Followup"))
samples_meta$Patient   <- factor(samples_meta$Patient)

# Create paired design matrix: ~ Patient + Condition
design <- model.matrix(~ Patient + Condition, data = samples_meta)

# 4. Run Limma-Trend on Log2-transformed Intensities

log2_intensities <- log2(intensity_matrix)

# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(log2_intensities, design)
fit <- eBayes(fit, trend = TRUE)

# Extract top differentially intense peaks (coefficient 7 is ConditionFollowup)

# This tests: Followup vs Baseline, accounting for patient-specific variation
results_table <- topTable(fit, coef = "ConditionFollowup", number = Inf, adjust.method = "BH")

summary(results_table$P.Value)
summary(results_table$adj.P.Val)

```

```{r, message=F, warning=F}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Define the p-value cutoffs and calculate peak counts
cutoffs <- c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05)

plot_data <- data.frame(
  Cutoff = factor(paste0("< ", cutoffs), levels = paste0("< ", cutoffs)),
  Count  = sapply(cutoffs, function(x) sum(results_table$P.Value < x))
)

# 2. Plot using ggplot2
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Cutoff, y = Count, fill = Cutoff)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE, fill = "#4C72B0") +
  # Add exact numbers above each bar
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(Count)), 
            vjust = -0.5, 
            fontface = "bold", 
            size = 4.5) +
  # Give extra vertical room so numbers aren't cut off at the top
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Peak Windows by P-Value Cutoff",
    x = "P-Value Threshold",
    y = "Number of Peak Windows"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black")
  )

```

### map to closest genes 



```{r, message=F, warning=F}
library(dplyr)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(ChIPseeker)
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)


# 1. Attach genomic coordinates from consensus_peaks using the row indices
peak_indices <- as.numeric(rownames(results_table))

results_with_coords <- results_table %>%
  mutate(
    seqnames = as.character(seqnames(consensus_peaks[peak_indices])),
    start    = start(consensus_peaks[peak_indices]),
    end      = end(consensus_peaks[peak_indices]),
    strand   = as.character(strand(consensus_peaks[peak_indices]))
  )

# 2. Filter for significant peaks (P.Value < 0.05)
sig_peaks_df <- results_with_coords %>% 
  filter(P.Value < 0.05)

cat(paste("Extracted", nrow(sig_peaks_df), "peaks with P.Value < 0.05\n"))

# 3. Convert to GRanges object
sig_peaks_GR <- GRanges(
  seqnames = sig_peaks_df$seqnames,
  ranges   = IRanges(start = sig_peaks_df$start, end = sig_peaks_df$end),
  strand   = sig_peaks_df$strand
)

# Attach statistical metadata columns
mcols(sig_peaks_GR) <- sig_peaks_df %>% dplyr::select(-seqnames, -start, -end, -strand)

# 4. Annotate peaks with nearest genes using ChIPseeker
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene

peak_annotation <- annotatePeak(
  sig_peaks_GR,
  TxDb = txdb,
  annoDb = "org.Hs.eg.db",    # Maps Entrez IDs to official Gene Symbols (e.g. BRCA1)
  tssRegion = c(-3000, 3000), # Promoter region definition (-3kb to +3kb of TSS)
  verbose = FALSE
)

# 5. Convert annotation output back to a Data Frame
annotated_df <- as.data.frame(peak_annotation)

# 6. Select and organize useful output columns
final_mapped_peaks <- annotated_df %>%
  dplyr::select(
    seqnames, start, end, width, logFC, AveExpr, P.Value,
    annotation,        # e.g., "Promoter (<=1kb)", "Distal Intergenic", "Intron"
    geneId,            # Entrez Gene ID
    SYMBOL,            # Official Gene Symbol (e.g., GAPDH)
    GENENAME,          # Full Gene Name
    distanceToTSS      # Exact distance in bp to nearest Transcript Start Site
  )

# 7. Save mapped results to CSV
#write.csv(final_mapped_peaks, "significant_peaks_mapped_to_genes.csv", row.names = FALSE)


# Preview top 5 mapped peaks
library(DT)
final_mapped_peaks%>%
  datatable(
    extensions = 'Buttons',
    caption = "", 
    options = list(
      dom = 'Blfrtip',
      buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
      lengthMenu = list(c(10, 25, 50, -1), c(10, 25, 50, "All"))
    )
  )
```



```{r, message=F, warning=F}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel) # For non-overlapping gene text labels

# 1. Identify top 10 most extreme genes to label on the plot
top_genes <- final_mapped_peaks %>%
  filter(!is.na(SYMBOL)) %>%
  arrange(P.Value) %>%
  head(10)

# 2. Generate Volcano Plot
ggplot(final_mapped_peaks, aes(x = logFC, y = -log10(P.Value))) +
  geom_point(aes(color = logFC > 0), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#2E8B57", "FALSE" = "#D95F02"),
    labels = c("TRUE" = "Gained", "FALSE" = "Lost"),
    name = "Peak Change"
  ) +
  # Add labels for top 10 genes
  geom_text_repel(
    data = top_genes,
    aes(label = SYMBOL),
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold",
    box.padding = 0.5,
    max.overlaps = 15
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Volcano Plot: Log2 Fold Change vs. Significance",
    x = "Log2 Fold Change (logFC)",
    y = "-log10 (P-Value)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

```{r, message=F, warning=F}
# 1. Calculate counts
sig_gained <- sum(final_results$P.Value < 0.05 & final_results$logFC > 0)
sig_lost   <- sum(final_results$P.Value < 0.05 & final_results$logFC < 0)

# 2. Assemble data frame with counts, percentages, and labels
pie_data <- data.frame(
  Direction = factor(c("Gained (logFC > 0)", "Lost (logFC < 0)"), 
                     levels = c("Gained (logFC > 0)", "Lost (logFC < 0)")),
  Count = c(sig_gained, sig_lost)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(Count / sum(Count) * 100, 1),
    Label = paste0(scales::comma(Count), "\n(", Percentage, "%)")
  )

# 3. Draw the Pie Chart
ggplot(pie_data, aes(x = "", y = Count, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white", size = 1.2) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", start = 0) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = Label), 
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), 
    color = "black", 
    fontface = "bold", 
    size = 5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Gained (logFC > 0)" = "#2E8B57", "Lost (logFC < 0)" = "#D95F02")) +
  theme_void(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Significant Peak Windows (P.Value < 0.05)",
    fill = "Peak Change"
  ) +

    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 10)),
```

## direct combine peak windows 



```{r, message=F, warning=F}
library(rtracklayer)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(ggVennDiagram)
library(ggplot2)

sample_names <- c("IF03_BL", "IF03_FU", "IF04_BL", "IF04_FU", 
                  "IF05_BL", "IF05_FU", "IF06_BL", "IF06_FU", "IF07_BL", "IF07_FU", "IF08_BL", "IF08_FU")
names(peak_files) <- sample_names

# 3. Read files into GRanges lists
cat("Importing narrowPeak files...\n")
gr_list <- lapply(peak_files, function(x) import(x, format = "narrowPeak"))

# 4. Filter for high-confidence peaks using native R looping (Prevents structure corruption)
p_cutoff_log10 <- -log10(0.05)
cat("Filtering individual sample peaks for p-value <= 0.05...\n")

filtered_gr_list <- list()
for (name in sample_names) {
  current_gr <- gr_list[[name]]
  # Filter strictly using native GRanges subsetting
  filtered_gr_list[[name]] <- current_gr[mcols(current_gr)$pValue >= p_cutoff_log10]
}

# 5. Combine the 4 Baseline samples together and the 4 Follow-up samples together
cat("Merging condition groups into unified Baseline and Follow-up peak sets...\n")

# Use BiocGenerics::append or explicit c() on clean GRanges components
baseline_stacked <- c(
  filtered_gr_list[["IF03_BL"]], 
  filtered_gr_list[["IF04_BL"]], 
  filtered_gr_list[["IF05_BL"]], 
  filtered_gr_list[["IF06_BL"]],
  filtered_gr_list[["IF07_BL"]],
  filtered_gr_list[["IF08_BL"]]
)
baseline_combined <- GenomicRanges::reduce(baseline_stacked)

followup_stacked <- c(
  filtered_gr_list[["IF03_FU"]], 
  filtered_gr_list[["IF04_FU"]], 
  filtered_gr_list[["IF05_FU"]], 
  filtered_gr_list[["IF06_FU"]],
  filtered_gr_list[["IF07_FU"]],
  filtered_gr_list[["IF08_FU"]]
)
followup_combined <- GenomicRanges::reduce(followup_stacked)

# 6. Generate an absolute master list of unique windows across both conditions
master_consensus <- GenomicRanges::reduce(c(baseline_combined, followup_combined))
cat("Total master peak windows identified:", length(master_consensus), "\n")
```




```{r, message=F, warning=F}
# 1. Install and Load the ggvenn package 
# install.packages("ggvenn")
library(ggvenn)


cutoff=500

# findOverlaps with minoverlap handles the length constraint natively at the genomic layer
baseline_overlaps <- findOverlaps(master_consensus, baseline_combined, minoverlap = cutoff)
followup_overlaps <- findOverlaps(master_consensus, followup_combined, minoverlap = cutoff)

# Extract the master consensus peak index IDs that match the criteria
baseline_ids  <- unique(queryHits(baseline_overlaps))
followup_ids <- unique(queryHits(followup_overlaps))

# Structure the input data into a clean two-group named list
venn_data <- list(
  "Baseline Peaks"  = baseline_ids,
  "Follow-up Peaks" = followup_ids
)

# 8. Generate and save the horizontal side-by-side Venn Diagram
cat("Plotting horizontal Venn Diagram...\n")

p <- ggvenn(
  venn_data, 
  fill_color = c("#c7e9b4", "#f07167"), # Left circle: Soft Mint | Right circle: Soft Coral
  stroke_size = 1.0,                    # Circle border thickness
  set_name_size = 5,                    # Text size for "Baseline Peaks" and "Follow-up Peaks"
  text_size = 5                         # Text size for counts inside circles
) +
  labs(
    title = "Chromatin Accessibility Window Comparison",
    subtitle = "Venn Diagram: Peaks Passing 5% FDR Cutoff (>500bp Overlap Required)"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30", margin = margin(b = 15))
  )

# Render the plot horizontally to your Viewer
print(p)
```

```{r, message=F, warning=F}
baseline_unique_ids <- setdiff(baseline_ids, followup_ids)

# IDs in Follow-up but NOT in Baseline (Gained peaks)
followup_unique_ids <- setdiff(followup_ids, baseline_ids)

# IDs found in both groups (Shared peaks)
shared_ids <- intersect(baseline_ids, followup_ids)


###########################################################

baseline_unique_peaks <- master_consensus[baseline_unique_ids]
followup_unique_peaks <- master_consensus[followup_unique_ids]
```

```{r, message=F, warning=F}

###########################################################
# 2. Extracting Gene Vectors for Network Profiling
###########################################################

# Isolate unique Entrez Gene IDs, filtering out any unmapped slots
genes_lost   <- unique(df_baseline$geneId[!is.na(df_baseline$geneId)])
genes_gained <- unique(df_followup$geneId[!is.na(df_followup$geneId)])

# Format into a structured named list for comparative profiling
biomarker_clusters <- list(
  "Lost_Chromatin_Marks"   = genes_lost,
  "Gained_Chromatin_Marks" = genes_gained
)


###########################################################
# 3. Comparative Pathway Enrichment (GO / KEGG)
###########################################################

# Run Gene Ontology (GO) Biological Processes comparative test
go_comparison <- compareCluster(geneClusters = biomarker_clusters, 
                                fun = "enrichGO", 
                                OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, 
                                ont = "BP", 
                                pAdjustMethod = "BH", 
                                pvalueCutoff = 0.05, 
                                qvalueCutoff = 0.05)
library(DT)
as.data.frame(go_comparison)%>%
datatable(extensions = 'Buttons',
          caption = "", 
            options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                           buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                           lengthMenu = list(c(10,25,50,-1),
                                             c(10,25,50,"All"))))

# Save statistical summary calculations
#write.csv(as.data.frame(go_comparison), "biomarker_pathway_enrichment_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
